payload.text: World coordinates are a 3D Cartesian system with the camera's pinhole as origin and the Z axis perpendicular to the camera's sensing plane.
World coordinates provide a fixed 3D reference frame to describe points relative to the camera, essential for mapping and projection.

- World coordinates. Let the origin of a World Cartesian coordinate system be the camera's pinhole. The coordinates of 3D position of a point, $\mathbf{P}$, in the world will be $\mathbf{P} = (X, Y, Z)$, where the Z axis is perpendicular to the camera's sensing plane (projection plane).

payload.prompt: What's the defining property of a world-coordinate frame in computer vision?
choices: It's attached to the camera and moves when the camera moves
It's a fixed reference frame for the scene, independent of any camera
It always has its origin at the image center
payload.explanation_correct: Right — world coordinates are anchored to the scene, so the same 3D point has the same coordinates regardless of where the camera is.
payload.explanation_wrong: Camera-coordinates move with the camera. World-coordinates are the *other* frame — the one that stays put.
